newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hardie sees much higher year profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hardie sees much higher year profit.

text.p: Building products group James Hardies Industries Ltd said on Thursday that it should record a significantly higher profit this year if current trading conditions prevail in its key markets.

"Overall the company is doing well. If current trading conditions prevail in our key markets, we will record a significantly higher profit this year," James Hardie chairman John Reid said in a speech prepared for the annual meeting.
Reid said the first three months of the current financial year, which began on April 1, had produced good results.

"In Australia, there are some signs of an emerging recovery in housing construction and in the other markets our businesses service," he said. Fibre cement and pipelines divisions were currently ahead of the company's projections, while windows and building systems operations were tracking much as expected.

"Results from the Australian pipelines business, which recorded a large loss last year, are particularly pleasing. The business has already returned to profit and we are confident of a much improved result this year," Reid said.

In the United States, sales and profits from the gypsum business were good, while in fibre cement the company was on track for another year of very strong growth in sales and profits, and further cost and efficiency gains, he said.
James Hardie reported a net profit of A$83.0 million for the year to March 31, up from A$32.2 million in 1995/96.

Reid said the company had sold a number of substantial operations and assets and had enhanced the company's position as the leading fibre cement producer in the United States. Total cash proceeds from divestments totalled A$446.9 million.
"While fibre cement is our core business, we are also developing complementary businesses, such as gypsum and building systems," Reid said.
"These businesses provide opportunities to expand the market for fibre cement as well as being sustantial in their own right," he said.
